Subject: Severe p99 spikes + request buildup during peak promos

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

We saw two short windows yesterday (09:05–09:12 PT and 14:50–14:56 PT) where checkout API throughput collapsed and p99 latency jumped to ~18s. During those windows our monitoring shows a pileup of requests queued on your side and an elevated 502 rate from the routing layer. Customers were affected for ~6–8 minutes per window.

Attached is a log bundle and a representative request batch. We haven't changed client-side retry behavior; the pattern looks like server-side queueing/backpressure rather than a retry storm, but we don't have access to server metrics. This is high customer impact (large promo day for Atlas). Can you confirm receipt and next steps? We need a timeline for mitigation and an exec sync if this is going to take longer than a day.

Thanks,
Maya
Customer Ops | Atlas Retail

Subject: Re: Severe p99 spikes + request buildup during peak promos

Quick notes from infra review (first-pass):

Observations:
- During both windows we observed a large number of inflight requests staging on the worker pool scheduler. The scheduler's pending queue length increased sharply and then drained in bursts.
- The customer is on a recent model variant (v2-int8) that we rolled out two days ago to ~10% of traffic. That variant has ~2.3x memory working set for KV cache population compared to the previous default.
- Concurrency limiter (per-customer gate) had an emergency cap of 128 active requests at the time; our traffic generator tests expect 1024 for this account in promo scenarios. The cap was set lower as part of an automated safety rule when we detected VM memory pressure on 2027-06-28.
- Autoscaler did not trigger quickly enough because the scheduling bottleneck was on the per-process request queue; new workers spun up but incoming requests still queued at gateway due to the limiter and lock contention.

Probable causal chain:
1) v2-int8 increases KV cache population per worker -> higher memory footprint.
2) Automated safety reduced per-customer concurrency cap to 128 to avoid OOM on constrained hosts.
3) During traffic spike the cap created a hard funnel, queueing requests and increasing p99.
4) Autoscaler and placement recovered slowly because the gating point was earlier in the request path and contend locks slowed worker startup.

Immediate mitigations executed:
- Raised Atlas concurrency cap to 1024 for the duration of the promo window (rolled at 09:40 PT).
- Rolled back v2-int8 variant from % traffic for Atlas to the previous stable variant (rolled starting 10:10 PT).
- Forced a soft restart of scheduler processes on the affected cluster to clear contention.

Next steps (actionable):
- Follow-up RCA item: prevent automated safety rules from setting per-customer caps without a cross-check on expected traffic (INF-4521).
- Engineering action: add early detection metric for KV cache per-worker growth and a preemptive scale trigger.
- Product: re-evaluate rollout canary size for memory-sensitive variants.

Assigning:
- Infra: Dylan to lead scheduler contention fix and tests (due 2027-07-07).
- Platform: Ben to own safety rule exceptions and a short-term whitelist for known accounts (due 2027-07-05).
- CS: Marissa to coordinate exec comms and offer credit if customer requests (due 2027-07-02).

Ben
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Severe p99 spikes + request buildup during peak promos — interim RCA and next steps

Maya — thanks again for flagging this and for the log bundle. Summary of what we found and next steps below.

Executive summary (for Atlas execs):
- Root cause: an automated safety rule reduced Atlas’ per-customer concurrency cap to 128 after host memory pressure on 2027-06-28. Combined with a recent model variant (v2-int8) that increases per-worker KV cache population, this created a bottleneck during short promo spikes. Requests queued at the gateway and p99 latency spiked until we raised the cap and rolled back the variant.
- Mitigation completed: cap raised to 1024, v2-int8 traffic for Atlas rolled back, scheduler processes restarted. Customer impact window ~2x ~6–8 minute spikes; no data loss.
- Risk: if other large accounts are on memory-heavier variants the safety rule could trigger again.

Actions and timeline:
- Today (complete): temporary cap increase and variant rollback; postmortem draft attached.
- 2027-07-05: safety rule exception mechanism + whitelist for known high-QPS accounts (owner: Ben).
- 2027-07-07: scheduler contention patch and integration tests (owner: Dylan).
- 2027-07-12: rollout policy update for memory-sensitive variants and canary gating (owner: Product).

Customer-facing offer: Marissa will run a quick exec sync with Atlas and propose a one-month service credit as a gesture (Marissa, can you confirm acceptance and timing?).

If you want we can schedule a 30-minute readout with engineering leadership tomorrow 10:00 PT to walk through the fixes and answer exec questions.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll follow up with a final postmortem once the engineering items land.

Regards,
Soojin
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
